## Start with one representative question

[S01-Q010](#S01-Q010)

<p>Compare IEnumerable and IQueryable from an execution perspective. For a filtering pipeline, how would you determine when and where its operations run?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Predict where and when a query runs and whether its terminal operation matches the result contract.</p>

<ul>
<li>Distinguish sequence/provider behavior from the exposed interface.</li>
<li>Trace deferred construction, execution and materialization.</li>
<li>Choose terminal operators for zero, one and multiple matches.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>A pipeline description is not yet proof of when work runs. Follow it to the operation that requests a result, then test how many matches the caller permits; execution and cardinality together define the observable query contract.</p>

### S02-Q026 · Mechanism

<p>What are deferred execution and query translation, and how would you trace them in one LINQ query?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q026](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q026)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q026](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q026)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain deferred execution and query translation.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Deferred execution concerns when work occurs; translation concerns how an expression is converted for another execution engine. Separate query construction from observing actual execution.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Trace query construction, execution and provider translation boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State LINQ source, .NET/EF Core version and provider; inspect official translation rules and real command evidence rather than assuming every expression translates.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Identify an execution trigger and trace repeated enumeration.</li>
<li>Use a translatable and a potentially unsupported expression to explain verification.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming constructing a query already ran it or every C# operation becomes SQL.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What changes if the underlying data changes before enumeration?</li>
<li>How would you verify whether an expression ran locally or in the database?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare `IEnumerable` and `IQueryable` from an execution perspective.

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Trace query construction, enumeration and materialization. A provider is the component interpreting a query; its capabilities must be established rather than assumed.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Predict query execution and verify the provider boundary.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the sequence source, provider and framework version; check official provider documentation before claiming translation or evaluation behavior.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Distinguishes the exposed interface from the actual source and traces a terminal operation.</li>
<li>Checks generated commands or local execution with an example instead of assuming that every IQueryable means SQL.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Saying IEnumerable always runs eagerly in memory or IQueryable always runs in a database.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What evidence would show that a filter ran after materialization?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q024"></a>

### S02-Q024 · Application

<p>How would you choose among First, FirstOrDefault, Single and SingleOrDefault for a query with a stated cardinality contract?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q024](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q024)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q024](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q024)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare `First`, `FirstOrDefault`, `Single`, and `SingleOrDefault`.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Cardinality is the expected number of matching elements. Explain zero, one and multiple matches, and connect the operator choice to the meaning of unexpected data.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose a terminal operator from expected result count and failure semantics.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify in-memory LINQ versus an EF provider, element type and ordering; verify official API/provider behavior before claiming generated SQL or cost.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Compare all four operators on zero, one and multiple matches.</li>
<li>Explain which data problem should be visible and how to test it.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Choosing solely by shorter syntax or treating OrDefault as a guarantee that all failures disappear.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What does first mean when your query has no explicit order?</li>
<li>Would operator choice enforce uniqueness in the database?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A hypothetical lookup expects either a missing item or one unique item. Build a LINQ pipeline over a named provider, choose a terminal operation, and predict zero, one and two matches. Locate any materialization boundary and propose command/output checks under the stated provider version.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains deferred execution and predicts a terminal operation’s boundary cases.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Checks the actual provider and location of evaluation while defending the cardinality requirement.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>An IQueryable declaration or one successful lookup does not prove translation or uniqueness handling.</p>
